featured_reviews.name: Ketki Yash
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved this café! I tried their Bravacado toast which came with delicious sweet potato fries, and the Sabbaba wrap with salad and fries on the side — both were super fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. I was so excited to dig in that I actually forgot to take a photo of the wrap! 😄

Ended the meal with their Hum Dark Chocolate Cake, and it was rich, moist, and just the right amount of sweet. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the overall vibe of the place was great.

Definitely going back soon to try their salads and bowls — if they’re anything like what I had today, I’m sure they’ll be amazing!

featured_reviews.name: Dinesh Katke
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just had a fantastic meal at Project Hum. If you think healthy eating means compromising on taste, this place will change your mind.

Chocolate Smoothie: Mind-blown that this is sugar-free! It was rich and perfectly sweet; you’d never guess it was the healthier choice.

Spiced Grilled Chicken Breast: Hand down the best chicken breast I’ve ever had. Super juicy and perfectly cooked. The "Hum green paste" on top is a game changer.

Sides: The sweet potato fries and sprouts salad were fresh and delicious.

Vibe & Service:
The ambience is great and the staff are incredibly polite. A huge plus for the clean and hygienic washrooms. It’s also pet-friendly.
Note: Parking can be a bit tricky, so plan accordingly. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Cocktail King
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found it overrated. Was looking forward to the farm to table concept. We ordered 3 sandwiches - Prawn Ghee Roast, Korean Chicken & Broc n Roll. We also ordered 3 mango milkshakes. Service was non existent. No water served. We ordered our food at the counter which is ok. Sandwiches took 30+ minutes. We asked for menu several times but were given one after we had finished eating. This took away anything else that we would have ordered since we didnt have menus.

Coming to the food. The Sour Dough used for the sandwiches was just too chewy. Our jaws started hurting (no exaggeration) trying to finish them. We were in no mood to complain as we were already late and noone in the restaurant seemed bothered about it anyway. The Korean chicken sandwich tasted off. The flavours didnt go well with the sour dough. Should have been in a milk bun. The fries were excellent! The milk shake again was just ok. Nothing special.

The meal felt very expensive (I know its Bandra) for the over quality of food.

Hope they get better.

Also love their sweet potato fries always a great add-on.

featured_reviews.name: Riya satra
featured_reviews.review_text: Its a cute little cafe in bandra. I ordered bravocado open toast with sweet potato fries and their new wrap Thai it up with sweet potato fries both the dishes were amazing full of flavours. Thai it up wrap was super juicy and saucy the wrap had good quantity of tofu in it amazing for the price but its a bit spicy yet very yummy. The bravocado open toast was just amazing good portion of guacamole on it and the sweet potatoe fries were my favourite super cripsy pairs so well with their in house sauce. The green tea lemon mojito was also good although it had less flavour of green tea felt more like lemonade. Overall 8/10 the only drawback is that the place is small and has long queues on the weekends after 7pm. The food also takes a while to arrive at your table like i waited 35mins for my wrap but the food was amazing.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!

featured_reviews.name: Omkar More
featured_reviews.review_text:
I hae been a regular at EAC since 2019. It has been my go-to for years, and while it remains a staple in my Bandra circuit, have noticed some shifts lately that are hard to ignore.
The freshness of their ingredients is honestly amazing - you can taste the quality in every bite. Over the years, I have tried almost everything on the menu across all sections, except for their new bread menu and the salads.
​The Food Journey
​When it comes to the food, I have had nearly all their desserts. If they have the Opera Pastry, it is a absolute must-try. On the other hand, the Tiramisu was just average. If you're going for a drink, the Pineapple Coriander Cooler and the Spiced Mojito are my absolute favorites, but the Vietnamese Cold Coffee is extremely bad - a hard skip.
For mains, their Chicken Burgers, especially the Peri Peri and Grilled Chicken, are top-notch. The Paneer Roasted Veggie Sandwich is also amazing. If you are there for breakfast, the Eggs Benedict is definitely the highlight.
​Pro Tip: You have to try their Roast Chicken with Mashed Potatoes; it is easily their most famous and iconic dish. Hard skip - anything fish.
However, lately, I have noticed the quality seems to have taken a dip. It is not a massive drop, but they have been increasing their SKUs (adding more items), and it is hard not to notice that the consistency isn't what it used to be.
The seating layout here is easily the best of any cafe in Bandra, but a recent experience with the crowd has made me think about stopping my visits completely.
​We were sitting near a table that was loud - uncomfortably loud. A man accompanied by two ladies spent hours shouting. It started with "India vs. Pakistan" and how "we will decimate them," then moved to "India vs. USA" and how the USA is so much better. It turned ugly when he started shitting on Hinduism, calling it a "pagan religion" and preaching Christianity. He kept saying India is "poor, filthy, and bad" because of Hindus and that people should go to churches to "get civilized."
It was highly uncomfortable and left us feeling genuinely shook. I took three weeks to think about whether I should even post this, but the experience was that bad.

Time to hunt for a new go to place.

Cafe Goencho, Pali Hill is an absolute Goan food heaven! 🌴🔥 From the moment you walk in, the cozy, old-school Goan vibe wraps you in warmth and nostalgia — it feels like stepping straight into a Goan home kitchen.

The Poieto here is the real show-stopper — rich, soulful, and packed with deep, authentic flavors. Slow-cooked to perfection, it’s comforting, hearty, and incredibly satisfying. This is the kind of dish that stays with you long after the meal ends. Truly outstanding and a must-try for anyone who loves traditional Goan cuisine.

The rest of the menu is just as impressive. The curries are bold yet beautifully balanced, the seafood is fresh and perfectly cooked, and every dish tastes like it’s been made with love and generations of culinary wisdom. Each bite feels authentic, homely, and full of character.

Tasted like frozen prawns in tomato ketchup. Overall, I'd definitely visit again for the Poietos.

Additionally, one of the staff members was seen behaving in an unhygienic manner while on duty, which was very uncomfortable and concerning, especially in a food service environment. The staff was unprofessional and did not handle the situation properly.

featured_reviews.name: Natasha Rajani
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place honestly serves some of the worst food I’ve had in a long time. I ordered a tandoori soya chaap roll and a shahi chicken roll, and both tasted exactly the same. Same chutney, same filling, no difference at all. It makes you wonder why they even have different items on the menu.
Both rolls were ridiculously spicy to the point where you couldn’t taste anything else. There was no mention of this anywhere. No balance, no flavor, just overpowering spice. At one point I actually started feeling dizzy because of how extreme the spice was and had to throw the food away.

Paying 350 for something like this is a complete waste of money. It feels careless and poorly made, like no real thought has gone into the food.
Just avoid this place. There are plenty of better options that actually care about what they’re serving.

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Salim Shahi Sigdi at Pali Hill, Bandra West, is a true gem, bustling with excitement from evening until late into the night. A favorite among celebrities, this spot serves up mouthwatering Mughlai, Chinese, and traditional dishes. The mutton seekh kebabs are a midnight treat, while the Shahi Tikka Chicken, with its rich dahi, and the creamy Afghani Chicken are simply delicious. The Paneer Tikka is also worth a try, but my personal favorite was the Chicken Baida Roti. Everything was fantastic—10/10. If you’re in Pali Hill, this place is a must-visit

featured_reviews.name: hansa bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Suzette has become my go-to spot for coffee, and it’s easy to see why. The moment you walk in, the open, airy feel of the place puts you at ease — it’s the kind of café you actually want to linger in.
What really sets Suzette apart is the people. The staff are warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming, and the owner is just as friendly — the kind of person who makes you feel like a regular from day one. Great service here isn’t an afterthought, it’s the whole vibe.
Beyond the excellent coffee, the food is well worth exploring. The sandwiches are satisfying and well-made, and the crêpes are a must-try. Whether you’re stopping in for a quick cup or settling in for a proper bite, Suzette delivers every time. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Sakshi shrivastava
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited Suzette in Bandra West for the first time, all the way from Vadodara, and had a truly wonderful experience. Though we had only ordered omelettes, the café manager, Aarif, surprised us with a complimentary cappuccino and also offered us a taste of both sweet and savoury crepes on the house. It was such a thoughtful gesture and made our visit even more special. The food was absolutely delicious, and the entire team—from the chef to the staff and manager—was incredibly warm and welcoming. We highly recommend this place for both the taste and the hospitality!

featured_reviews.name: Varun Badhwar

Ambience: It was nice but too small and literally had little to no space to stand. In winters outside sitting would be lovely and otherwise inside would be the best option

featured_reviews.name: Merlyn
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had originally checked with Soul Fry for their karaoke nights, but the owner mentioned that reservations usually need to be made around 10 days to 2 weeks in advance. Later, we ended up going there for lunch on one of the days. I had even called beforehand to ask if reservations were necessary, and he said yes, definitely. But when we actually reached, the restaurant was pretty empty.

The food was good — nothing extremely standout, but overall decent. One thing we did feel though was that everything was slightly on the pricier side for what was offered. That being said, the interiors really give you that old-school Goan tavern vibe, which added a nice charm to the experience.

featured_reviews.name: george joseph
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find. A cute little restaurant with goan vibes right in bandra. You would need to plan to be there around opening time if you want to get a seat in their cozy indoor area. They close for the evening making it a little exclusive with the time restriction. The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Ashwinth Naveen
featured_reviews.review_text: My first time in Mumbai, and I have absolutely no regrets choosing Soul Fry as my go-to spot! The karaoke night was an absolute blast and made the whole experience even more memorable. The vibe, music, and overall atmosphere were amazing, and I genuinely had such a great time. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip — would love to visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Marlyn Pereira
featured_reviews.review_text: If you’re into authentic Goan food this is a great place to be. They have karaoke in the evenings and is usually packed so you might have to book in advance, or take only outside seating. The bombil fry and pompfret rechado is a must try.

Since food and drink make parties pop, we got our culinary hermano from México City, Chef Pablo on board. He makes sure real flavours from Baja all the way to Yucatan land up on your plate and glass. Steeped in the nation's pulsing present with a healthy dash of its awesome Mexican heritage, Mezcalita is the taste of México

Mini punjab brings back childhood memories back to life. Had a great meal at Mini Punjab after multiple reviews seen lately of bad food & service. I still took my chance & visited the place. The restaurant is known for its rich North Indian food and generous portions. Butter chicken fish Amritsari are to drool for . I ordered the classic butter chicken fish Amritsari & roti.
Thankfully from the time I entered was greeted with a Smile from the uncle at the entrance.
Service was quick and staff were courteous even during busy hours.
The ambience is family-friendly ot fancy but jst right for casual dinners and late-night cravings .A solid choice if you want hearty North Indian food in Bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Sneha Lenze
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a great meal at Mini Punjab. The restaurant is known for its rich North Indian food and generous portions.  Though their non veg section are famous, with that classic Punjabi taste; being a vegetarian I had my comfort food including Roti and Veggies.Service was quick and staff were courteous even during busy hours. The ambience is simple and family-friendly, making it a reliable spot for casual dinners and late-night cravings in Bandra. A solid choice if you want hearty North Indian food in Mumbai.

Yeah. no more.

featured_reviews.name: Keshav Murugesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a regular at Kitchen Garden, Bandra, and wanted to share a consistent issue I’ve experienced over a few visits.

The café is listed as opening at 7:30 AM, and I’ve stopped by a few times around then after morning workouts. However, each time, the team has still been in the middle of setting up—cleaning, switching on machines—and not ready to serve even a simple coffee. If 7:30 AM is the stated opening time, it would be reasonable to expect at least basic service from then. Otherwise, it may be more accurate to list the opening time as 8:00 AM.

More importantly, on a couple of occasions, the person managing the morning shift (appears to be a lady dressed in black in a supervisory role) has responded in a rather abrupt and not very welcoming manner—almost as if customers are interrupting the opening process. It came across as dismissive, and at times borderline rude. This is what prompted me to finally write this.

I enjoy the space and have otherwise had good experiences here, which is why I hope this feedback is taken constructively. A more prepared and welcoming start to the day would make a big difference, especially given the number of early-morning visitors in the neighbourhood.

We visited as a group of six, including two kids, and loved everything we ordered—corn dog, veg and mushroom gyoza, tofu katsu curry, and mushroom and prawn takoyaki. The food was fresh, delicious, reasonably priced, service was excellent, toilets are available, though parking can be tricky.

Getting a good seat can be a challenge if you’re in a group of 4 and above. The indoor setting can sit just about 7 to 8 people so most of the times you’ll have to sit outside and face the heat and mosquitoes.

featured_reviews.name: Arshad Mir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Brunched at MAG St. Bandra recently and as someone who’s eaten through enough of Bombay’s brunch circuit to know when a place is pure hype versus when there’s actual substance behind the aesthetic — MAG St definitely falls in the latter category. The food is genuinely good. The problem? They’ve started pricing like they’re in Notting Hill or Le Marais.

Started strong with the watermelon feta salad — fresh, balanced and properly refreshing, though ice-cold watermelon would’ve taken it up another notch in Bombay heat. The dim sums were fair play overall. The truffle edamame dumplings were decent but forgettable, while the shrimp in ginger broth dumplings were the clear standout. That broth/sauce situation was excellent.

The Asian fried rice was honestly a surprise hit. Comforting, flavourful, generous enough portion-wise — though realistically this is a ₹550 dish masquerading as an ₹825 one because Bandra brunch economics require everything to sound “premium” enough for the Bandra aunties and influencer crowd.

Then came the smoked salmon eggs benedict — the dish everyone seems to post here. It was alright. Not bad by any means, but I’ve definitely had better at Sarabeth's. The hollandaise was absolutely drenched over the eggs to the point it overpowered everything else a bit.

The real stars? The drinks. Phenomenal. Especially the Summer Thirst — probably the best thing we ordered all afternoon.

Bill came to around ₹5.4k for two (roughly £42 / €49), which honestly could and probably should have landed closer to ₹4k. But then again, this is Bandra in 2026 — people here are happily paying London and Paris brunch prices while sitting off Linking Road, so fair play to MAG St for understanding their market perfectly.

Overall: stylish spot, genuinely solid kitchen, not just Instagram fluff — but you’re definitely paying a Bandra premium on top of the food.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally checked off Mag St. Café in Bandra from my must-try list with a spontaneous lunch on 31st December. Despite not having a reservation, the hostess graciously seated us right away, setting the tone for a relaxed meal.

We kicked things off with the meatball bolognese, which was rich, flavourful, and genuinely delicious. The highlight, however, was the buff steak — the manager’s recommendation of medium-rare was spot on. It arrived perfectly cooked, juicy and tender, easily one of the best steak preparations in the city.

The vibe is warm and inviting with a great ambience. The staff were attentive, friendly and helpful throughout

Parking in the Bandra can be challenging, so plan a bit of extra time if you’re driving in.

Priced on the higher side ₹2,700 for two, which feels fair for the quality and portions

Coming back definitely to explore more from the menu!

featured_reviews.name: Madan Dedhia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mag St. Bandra is a culinary gem! This wonderful cafe is perfect for any meal of the day - breakfast, brunch, lunch, or dinner. The cozy and comfortable ambiance makes it an ideal spot to relax and enjoy delicious food. Be prepared for a crowd at lunchtime, but don't let that deter you!

The service is top-notch, with attentive and friendly staff. The portions are generous, and the quality of food is excellent. Plus, the prices are reasonable, making it a great value for money.

We indulged in some amazing dishes, including the Edamame truffle dumpling, garlic bread, and hand-cut truffle fries - all were mouth-watering! The drinks menu impressed us too, with perfect cups of iced mocha and hot chocolate, alongside a refreshing coke.

Convenience-wise, valet parking is available, adding to the overall convenience.

Overall, Mag St. Bandra is a must-visit cafe in Bandra. Don't miss out on the delightful food, excellent service, and cozy atmosphere. Highly recommended!

Visited Good Flippin’ Burgers recently and had an average experience overall. The place has a nice, casual vibe and is quite popular, so it feels lively and service is fairly quick.

However, I found the menu to be quite limited, which was a bit disappointing as there weren’t too many options to choose from. The burgers looked good and the ingredients seemed fresh, but the taste didn’t really stand out for me—it felt a bit underwhelming and not something I’d go back craving.

featured_reviews.name: Eldred D’souza
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited GFP Bandra on Friday, 31st October, for our Halloween lunch. The atmosphere was great. It's a nice cozy little outlet. The lady at the counter, I'm sorry I didn't catch her name but she was wearing specs was one of the most courteous restaurant employees I've ever encountered. She was very sweet and welcoming and oozing genuine warmth. Thanks to her for making our experience memorable. The food was delicious. We ordered the chicken cluckinator, fries and the Kerfuffle. I've had similar burgers like the cluckinator from competitors but this one was really well cooked. The quantity of chicken was generous, crispy and juicy at the same time. Amazing. The fries were nice but the show stealer was the Kerfuffle Buff burger. Man was it amazing. Was so juicy and succulent. The cook on the patty was well done.

P.S.: Only wish the price would've been a little low. Overall a very good experience. The kerfuffle will bring me back often. ;)

featured_reviews.name: Ritesh Naik
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Good Flippin’ Burgers - Bandra with my friends on 12th February around 10:30 p.m. The ambience, seating arrangement, and music were really nice and created a great vibe. We tried the Chicken Clucker burger and Chicken Peri Peri Wings — the burger was absolutely amazing (5/5), but the wings were too spicy and had excess masala for our taste (3/5). The only downside was that the counter staff were not very welcoming, which slightly affected the overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: AHTESHAM ANSARI
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst and most overhyped place for burgers I've ever seen.
The AC was not working at all.
Tried their best selling cluckinator and buff smash. Both of them were low quality burgers for 350/400 Rs price and average size.
Better try Jimis or Frisbees.

featured_reviews.name: Adriel Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
A burger joint that actually lives up to the hype!

Good Flippin' Burgers is easily one of my top picks when it comes to a no-nonsense, satisfying burger experience. The patties are juicy, flavourful, and clearly made with care — no dry, overcooked nonsense here. The buns are soft yet hold everything together perfectly (no collapsing halfway through your meal!), and the balance of sauces, cheese, and toppings hits the sweet spot.

The fries are golden, crisp, and addictive, especially the Peri Peri ones; and if you’re into sides, their chicken tenders and absolutely superb. For me, it's the sides that actually steal the show.

What I also love is the consistency. Whether you're dining in or ordering in, the quality doesn't drop. Service is usually quick, and the vibe is casual, clean, and efficient, exactly what you want from a great burger spot.

Highly recommend the “The Clucknator” or the “The Koren Krossover Ckikin burger 456”.

Tried both their Flippinade flavours, Cranberry and Lemon. The cranberry was surprisingly refreshing and gets a solid 4/5 from me. The lemon was okay, not bad, but didn’t quite hit the same mark 3/5.

These folks don’t just flip burgers, they nail the.

featured_reviews.name: Prajwal Gulwe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good Flippin’ Burgers in Bandra is a no-nonsense spot that gets the basics of burgers right. The buns are soft yet sturdy, the patties are flavorful, and the sauces are balanced—though at times, they can be a bit lacking, making the burger slightly dry.

The sides, like Peri Fries and Atomic Tenders, are solid too. The ambiance is casual, with quick service that keeps things moving. It’s not a place for a gourmet experience, and I don’t think they’re claiming to be. It delivers exactly what you’d expect, reliably.

featured_reviews.name: Prem Pradhan
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re visiting Phoenix Kurla, the Cheese Boom Veg Burger is a must-try. It’s exactly what the name suggests—a total explosion of molten cheese the moment you take a bite. The patty is perfectly crunchy, and it’s one of the few veg burgers that actually feels indulgent. Pro-tip: Grab extra napkins, you’re going to need them!"

Best burgers in Kurla! The Cluckinator and Cheese Boom are legendary. Fresh ingredients, great sauces, and always worth the price. 5 stars for the flavor and the friendly staff."

The "Grilla": Mention the Peri-Peri rub and Jalapeno cheese sauce.
The "Cheese Boom": Mention the molten cheese center and the crunch.

Had the Grilla chicken burger at the Kurla outlet and it was flipping good. The chicken was juicy, well-marinated in Peri-Peri spices, and the Jalapeno cheese sauce added the perfect kick. Much better quality than your average food court burger. The brioche buns are super soft and held everything together perfectly

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had lunch at The Village Shop today with my husband and overall it was a good experience. The food was fresh, wholesome, and it’s definitely a great place for people with allergies, dietary restrictions, or specific food preferences.

There was one mix-up where potato was added instead of sweet potato mash in one of the dishes, but the team replaced it with exotic vegetables without any issue, which we appreciated.

The only area that could really improve is the service and ingredient awareness among the staff. Our waiter didn’t seem very well informed about the ingredients and communication could have been better, especially for a place that caters to special diets and allergies. He was also taking the order from behind the counter instead of coming to the table, which felt a little impersonal.

That said, it’s still a lovely place with great potential, and this feedback is only to help make the experience even better with more informed and attentive staff.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Firstly! It’s a bit inside so you might not find it easily! But the space is cute cozy and really nice! It’s a pet friendly space so you can take your pets there!
The service is great but they do take some time to get what you’ve ordered.
The foods quite good here for the price! I loved their hot chocolate the most! And their goey chocolate cake too. If you have a sweet tooth you might like to try out the dessert menu. Quite yum
Oh and yea! Their mushroom burger too was amazing.
Incase you’re with a big group you might have to reserve the space!

featured_reviews.name: Neeraja Sundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very ghastly and amusing experience at the Village Shop. I spent a Monday morning here, was hoping to get my coffee and breakfast  in some peace and quiet. It was only me in the cafe and the owner with 2 of her staff on another table.
In the first 10 mins I figured the owner had issues with staff, even though they spoke in hushed tones.

I let it slide. Naturally, I have no context of that conversation.
The food wasn’t up to the mark. They had it replaced without getting defensive.

Then, after a few mins I spoke loudly because I was on a call, and there was no one else in the cafe but me and the owner, I was asked to speak softly. She was irked. I gladly obliged.

I stepped outside to take my call. For 45 mins. In the heat. You see, I have been brought up with a lot of empathy.
It felt like my grandmother gave me a punishment to not enter the house.

What a ghastly experience for a Bandra cafe.  I hope the owners have the business acumen to start something else of their own. Customer centricity and empathy are not the strongest suit of some of the most affluent people in Bandra. What tarnishes reputation is lack of empathy for staff and no understanding of what customer focus looks like.

Money can’t buy you manners or class.

Its evident to me today, yet again :)
